newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks scramble to fresh highs by noon.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks scramble to fresh highs by noon.

text.p: SPI Futures 2591 +4 US 30yr cl 7.03 +0.04
10yrbond futs 92.410 -0.045 Gold NY 344.70 Lon fix 343.65
*Stocks move to fresh highs by midsession after offshore markets firm, BHP finds bottom. Volume 168.51 million, value A$309.53 million, 894 stocks traded, 315 steady, 343 up, 236 down.
The Australian share market eked out light gains to capture fresh highs by the midsession on Wednesday after offshore markets firmed.
By 12.00 p.m. (0200 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was up 8.1 points at 2,587.0, having touched a record high of 2,587.2, surpassing the previous record of 2,585.8 set on Tuesday.
June share price index futures were four points higher at 2,591, a four point premium to the index.
The lightly traded market eased in initial activity, but quickly settled in mildly positive territory as bellwether BHP found support at its lower levels.
"We were down early and are now up a few on the back of Wall Street but it's all fairly quiet," said a Brisbane-based dealer.
Others concurred, noting that the modest move to firmer ground had been underpinned by solid support for market leader BHP around the A$18.20 level.
"It has not been all that active," said a Sydney broker.
"BHP found a bottom and that has helped things in terms of the overall market."
BHP shares were three cents lower at A$18.36 by midday, having lost over six percent to today's low from Monday's high of A$19.42 prior to the fourth quarter profit warning.

Outside the leaders, personnel consultants Morgan and Banks Ltd posted a sharply higher full year net profit of A$9.97 million. Their shares were unchanged at A$8.20 with only three trades through by midday.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about three to two, while about 35 percent of stocks traded remained steady.

In other local markets, long Australian bond yields remained close to the day's highs after an initial burst of offshore selling, although the market is finding support at around current levels. By 12.35 p.m (0235 GMT), 10 year T-bonds were yielding 7.60 percent, up from Tuesday's 7.56 percent.
The Australian dollar tracked sideways to the midsession but the routine performance belied a backstage struggle as offshore sellers vied to break support.
By 12.35 p.m. (0235 GMT), the local currency was idling at US$0.7645/50 having ended Tuesday here at US$0.7650/55.
